abstract: Markman's secant-sheaf programme proves algebraicity of Weil classes on abelian $2n$-folds once a sheaf on an abelian $n$-fold, with Chern character on a secant line of the spinor variety, is semiregular. It works for genus-three Jacobians. By the Calabi–Yau adjunction, on abelian fourfolds the Buchweitz–Flenner map on $\mathrm{Ext}^2$ is the transpose of Hochschild evaluation. This gives a test on the Chern character alone: a simple fully semiregular sheaf satisfies $\chi(F,F)-2+2\,\mathrm{rk}\,c^1\le\mathrm{rk}\,c^2$, with equality for line bundles and the ideal sheaf of a point. For Markman's imaginary-quadratic secant characters, $\chi=8d^2|c|^2\Theta^4/4!>0$. So on every abelian fourfold, for every ample $\Theta$, no simple sheaf with such a character is fully semiregular, and Perry's $G$-semiregularity for free translation groups does not rescue them. For the weaker condition that Markman's argument actually uses (injectivity on the image of evaluation, i.e. $\ker\mathrm{ob}=\ker\mathrm{ch}$), both of his genus-four families fail as well. They cannot deform to first order transversally to the Jacobian locus: for the theta-divisor sheaves, a non-Cartier surface does not survive the smoothing of the nodes of $\Theta$; for the union ideals, Brill–Noether loci are rigid (Lombardi–Tirabassi). By Künneth the failure lifts to his product objects on $X\times\hat X$, along a direction tangent to the Weil period domain. So the mechanism with Brill–Noether seeds is special to genus three, where the Jacobian locus is open. A variant covers his real-multiplication construction when the Hilbert modular locus is transverse to the Jacobian locus, e.g. for genus-four curves with an order-five automorphism of branching type (1,2,3,4). A second, noncommutative obstruction holds on every principally polarized fourfold: a secant ideal sheaf with a reduced component of codimension at least three, or with two surface components meeting transversally, fails, which excludes Abel–Prym seeds. No new case of the Hodge conjecture is proved.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: v3 implements the corrections requested in the v2 acceptance review; no new results. (1) Theorem F: the Orlov functor is now displayed correctly, Φ = (id×Φ_P)^{-1}∘μ^*, i.e. the inverse of μ_*∘(id×Φ_P), as in [2, (10.1.3)]; the relative extension argument is unchanged. (2) The consequences of Theorem G (seed design, §7(d), §1 and abstract) keep its hypotheses: reduced components of codimension ≥ 3 smooth somewhere off the others, and transversal surface meetings. Nonreduced and embedded components are stated as untreated. Summaries of Corollary F′ keep its transversality hypothesis. (3) Order-five example: the weight argument needs each primitive character once in H⁰(K_C). Among branching types, (1,1,1,2) gives multiplicities (2,1,1,0), (1,1,4,4) is hyperelliptic, and (1,2,3,4) is the supported case, now stated as such; the contradictory sentence is removed. (4) Remark 7.1: its conclusion now agrees with Theorem G (the seeds fail). The twist solutions are labelled as examples, including m = −1 (a₂ = 1, d = 3, a₁ = 11, a₀ = 60 − ε). Scout's ℓ = 5 and conductor estimate are marked as reported, not proved here. (5) Heat equation: the coefficient for independent coordinates τ_jk, j ≤ k, is (2−δ_jk)/(4πi). Also: Corollary F′ now uses the direct argument that the factors' characters stay Hodge, not invariance of κ(E).

coauthors.contribution: Theorem G: independent discovery of the local obstruction for point components, extension to curve components, audit of the proof, and the rank computation rk ob² = 18 vs rk c² = 12; audit of the relative-Orlov/Künneth step in Theorem F.

title: A Chern-character test for semiregularity on abelian fourfolds, and the failure of Markman's imaginary-quadratic secant sheaves
